related_questions.question: What are the five most common mental disorders in children?

text_blocks.snippet: The five most common mental health disorders in children are Anxiety Disorders, Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), Depression, Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), and Oppositional Defiant Disorder (ODD). These disorders can significantly impact a child's daily functioning and development, highlighting the importance of early identification and intervention.
snippet_highlighted_words: Anxiety Disorders, Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), Depression, Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), and Oppositional Defiant Disorder (ODD)

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a little more detail about each:

list.title: Anxiety Disorders:
list.snippet: These include conditions like generalized anxiety disorder, separation anxiety, and social anxiety, affecting around 7% of children. Symptoms can include excessive worry, fear, and avoidance behaviors.

list.title: ADHD:
list.snippet: This neurodevelopmental disorder affects 6-9% of school-aged children and is characterized by difficulty concentrating, hyperactivity, and impulsivity.

list.title: Depression:
list.snippet: Childhood depression, affecting about 3% of children, involves persistent sadness, loss of interest in activities, and changes in sleep or appetite.

list.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder:
list.snippet: Affecting 1 in 36 children, ASD involves challenges in social communication and repetitive behaviors.

list.title: Oppositional Defiant Disorder:
list.snippet: Affecting 1-6% of children, ODD is characterized by defiant, hostile, and uncooperative behavior.
